pr3138.title: docs: epic-steward — #2314 rollup + S3 re-triage, #226 close-out re-audit
pr3138.body:
## Summary
- **Epic #2314 — flow b (rollup).** The `## STEWARD PROPOSAL 2026-08-08` was answered after **32 days** (option (a): r7 / PR #2654 discharges D6) and #2385 closed `completed`. Checklist ticked → **10/11**; #2321 is the sole open child. Recorded as **D10**, plus a terminal **A3** on `issue-2385.md`.
- **Epic #2314 — flow a (re-triage).** The resuming worker implemented S3's retained lever (b) and measured it **refuted on D5**. All three of its design questions classified **NOVEL**, so PR #2393 parks `fleet:design-proposed` behind a second package, whose three recommendations are advisory and stay pending until answered. `issue-2321.md` **A3** records the unblock, the measurement, and what survives either ruling.
- **New ledger finding F5** — the S3 acceptance gate is **unsatisfiable as written**, on two independent grounds (below).
- **Epic #226 — flow d (close-out re-audit).** All four claims of the 57-day park still hold, but its own recommended remedy is broken. Filed **#3137**; recorded as **F1**, with a correction to a 2026-07-15 ledger entry that asserted something false. Ask restated with a re-fire edge (`fleet:steward-proposal`), recommendation advisory, epic left open pending the answer.

## Test plan
- [x] Ruling distribution **verified live, not assumed** — #2321 unblocked (`fleet:queued`); #1969 body line 16 is `**Host:** linux`; #3023 carries `human:approved` + `fleet:opus`; `34c7f7f4` confirmed an ancestor of master `7567858e5`.
- [x] Every shader claim in the worker's NEEDS-DESIGN re-verified verbatim before triage: `c_lighting_to_trixel.glsl:228` (+ Metal twin `:163`), `ir_sun_shadow_sample.glsl:64`, `:107`, `:121`.
- [x] **The PR's negative control re-run independently** — arms A and D are byte-identical (`sha256 aebac301a0cf4d1f`), arm B differs (`d27a601314d52ae9`), so the refutation isolates to the outer taps alone.
- [x] #226's four claims re-measured against master: no new `docs/perf-reports/` entry; #1100 still CLOSED (2026-05-24); `perf-gate.yml` still has no threading cell; 9/9 children shipped.
- [x] F1 traced end to end: `g_cliOverrides.workerThreads_` has exactly two occurrences in `perf_grid` (`main.cpp:169` declaration, `:814` assignment) and **no read site**; no CLI→`WorldConfig` path exists anywhere; `job_manager.cpp:92` clamps `max(1, requested)`.
- [x] Citation check — all cited file paths resolve at base; `#2204`, `#2083`, `#3137` resolved via `gh` and match their described meaning.
- [x] Docs-only diff confirmed (`git diff --name-only` is entirely `.fleet/plans/`); cross-repo info-isolation scan clean (positive-controlled); no auto-closing keyword in the commit message (positive-controlled).

## Notes for reviewer

Two things in here are corrections to *prior fleet artifacts*, not to the workers, and are the parts most worth a second opinion:

1. **`D8`'s `(a)(b)(c)` and `D9`'s levers `(a)(b)` are different lettered sets.** The NEEDS-DESIGN cites D8 to license dropping D9's lever (b); D8's options are the finer-resolution *architecture* set (2048² / 3rd cascade / split retune), and D9 explicitly **retained** lever (b). That citation is the only one offered for question 2, which is why the question rides the package instead of being answered inline.

2. **The 2026-07-15 `issue-226.md` ledger entry asserted "the axis is live — the exe consumes it (`main.cpp:758`)".** It does not. `:758` is the `--grid-size` handler; the `--worker-threads` handler is at `:809-814` and writes a field nothing reads. That entry had dismissed the stale script comment as doc drift — the comment is in fact still literally true, and the live defect underneath it invalidates the very command the park told the human to run to decide criterion 2. A run would have reported ~parity across an inert axis and read as "≥2× refuted".

**F5's second ground is stated deliberately as a non-claim.** Side by side, the post-#2385 metric reads *less* clean than the pre-#2385 one (z2: components 88→157, largest_frac 0.88→0.2073). I did **not** record that as a regression: the 2026-07-14 capture that produced the older numbers states no ROI, and `render-shadow-metric.py --roi` is optional, so the two may cover different regions. The finding is that the gate has no ROI convention and therefore cannot be evaluated either way. It does not challenge D10 — option (a) was argued on cost-ceiling grounds, and this baseline was posted 44 minutes *after* the ruling.

No code is touched. No epic is closed. Both umbrellas carry `fleet:steward-proposal`, so both asks now have a defined re-fire edge — the thing #226 spent 57 days without.

## Amendment 2026-09-10 (fleet:needs-fix)

The reviewer flagged that the dated "no-rule fallback" clauses in the three plan
entries authorised a later steward to close issues, re-anchor acceptance
criteria, and file follow-up children if a human did not answer by a deadline.
That conflicts with the steward protocol, whose only resolution edge is a human
or architect answering inline and removing `fleet:steward-proposal` — silence is
not that edge. Verified against `epic-steward-protocol.md` (flow a: "**The
responder** … answers each question inline … and **removes**
`fleet:steward-proposal`. That removal is the re-fire edge") and the label
reference; there is no timed-fallback machinery anywhere in the protocol, and
even routing a package onward to the escalation-target is human-initiated.

Removed in this amendment: the fallback clauses in `issue-226.md`,
`issue-2314.md` and `issue-2321.md`, **and** the matching sections of the three
posted comments (#2314 issuecomment-5613956380, #226 issuecomment-5614036806,
#2393 issuecomment-5613961439), each of which now states plainly that the
recommendations are advisory and the package stays pending. Recommendations,
evidence, corrections and the re-fire edge are unchanged — only the self-granted
licence to act on silence is gone. The stall the clauses were reaching for (32
and 57 days unanswered) is recorded in both comments as an open fleet-protocol
question rather than solved locally.

Refs #2314, #226, #2321, #2385, #2393, #3137

commit_backticked:
fleet: don't treat a closing verb quoted in a code span as scope-shipped evidence (layer 5) (#1902)

* fleet: don't treat a closing verb quoted in a code span as scope-shipped evidence (layer 5)

`fleet-queue-ingest`'s scope-shipped pre-flight (`fleet_scope_shipped.py`)
mislabels a plan PR as having shipped the issue it plans when the plan's
body *quotes* the `Closes #N` that the future implementation PR will write.

Concrete case: #1824 <- PR #1854 ("docs: plan #1824 ..."). Layer 4 correctly
suppresses the plan-doc *title*, but #1854's body says:

    the structured plan for #1824 (... impl PR will carry the code + `Closes #1824`)
    Plan doc for #1824 -- does not close the issue (the implementation PR will)

The body closing-verb check matched that backticked, forward-referenced
`Closes #1824`, so the predicate returned True and the issue was wrongly
parked as scope-shipped (blocking it from the queue).

Layer 5: strip markdown code spans (fenced ``` blocks + inline `...`) from
the body before the closing-verb scan. A verb quoted in code is documentation,
not an action; a genuine ship writes `Closes #N` as prose, so the strip costs
no true positive. Spans collapse to a space so a span between letters can't
fuse into a spurious verb ("clo`x`ses" is not "closes").

Verified end-to-end: the predicate now returns False against the live #1854
body for #1824 (was True). 47 predicate tests + 30 queue-projection tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fleet: clarify layer-5 code-span comment (review nit)

Replace the ambiguous '(layer 4 → layer 5)' arrow notation — which
read as a layer transition rather than 'layer 5, closing a gap layer 4
missed' — with explicit wording: layer 5 strips code spans before the
closing-verb scan; layer 4 stopped title refs, not body code spans.

Addresses the sole nit on PR #1902 (reviewer-flagged, comment-only).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(fleet): epic-steward — #2544 P3 reconcile + A4/A5 + adopt #2669 (#2757)

Flow b on PR #2585 (merged 2026-08-01, master 4c4554d5), which closed
#2547 five minutes before the iteration started. Umbrella checklist
ticked; ledger reconciled-through moved to that merge.

The scope-drift audit found one real deviation from a steward amendment.
A2 asked for the ratified gate to be an analytic ray/surface assert PLUS
a center-pixel crop score. The crop was built and does not survive the
geometry: the pinned surface point rotates onto the limb at +/-90 deg, so
the crop straddles the silhouette edge — 42px of crop-centroid drift on
center-depth at zoom 4, scale-invariant. What shipped instead is a new
center-axis block whose probe axis lies on the viewport-center ray, so
the derived surface point IS the probe's axis point. Recorded as D7 and
restated for the epic bar as A4, not escalated: D5's substance was
honored and the substitution arrives with the measurement that forced it.

A4 also fixes a gate-vs-criteria contradiction A3 could not have seen.
center-column, center-depth and center-axis now emit FOCUS-OK rather than
PINNED — their silhouette deviation is reported, not gated — so the
umbrella's "all passes PINNED" closing criterion is unreachable as
literally worded. A4 restates the bar per block; the umbrella body is not
edited, per the checklist-only carve-out.

A5 re-validates P4 (#2548), whose PR #2659 is in flight. Its plan's
"depth-probe center derivation (Phase 3 helper)" now resolves to
IRRender::readbackCompositeDepth / decodeCompositeDepth, not a
prefab-side derivation — the pivot runs upstream of IRPrefab::DepthProbe,
which keeps its surface and delegates. A5 also carries forward the
latch-the-iso-depth-not-the-world-point lesson and its negative-control
test.

Adopts #2669 onto the checklist (flow c; fleet-validate-stack reports all
five children PASS with #2669 the sole drift item) with a STUB plan — it
is a contract amendment whose three options are different products, so it
must not be claimed before the ruling. Its question is this iteration's
proposal package on the umbrella; fleet:steward-proposal applied. Five
Findings now gate close-out: #2645 (the only red pass), #2641 (systematic
derive bias, cross-backend), #2669, the still-unowned jitter residual,
and the absent OpenGL-host verdict on #2576 and #2585.
